data.name: Ancharika
data.gender_notes: Ancharika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ancharika is a Sanskrit female name derived from the goddess Ancharani, the deity of wisdom and knowledge. In Hindu mythology, Ancharani is believed to bestow intelligence and knowledge upon her devotees. The name Ancharika is a tribute to this goddess and symbolizes wisdom, knowledge, and intelligence. The name Ancharika carries the meaning “Goddess of Knowledge” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ancharika usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of knowledge and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Ancharika belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Knowledge.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ancharika total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Ancharika is a Hindu name mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Sanskrit epic of India. She is the wife of Bhishma Pitamaha and is also known as Satyavati. Ancharika is mentioned as the mother of Vidura.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India, the other being the Ramayana. It narrates the story of the Kurukshetra war between two groups of cousins belonging to the Kuru Dynasty.

historical_references.reference: Ancharika is also mentioned in the Puranas, a set of ancient Hindu texts. She is the daughter of the sage Angiras and is married to the sage Gautama Muni. Ancharika is known as Ahalya, a famous character in Hindu mythology who was cursed to turn into a stone by her husband Gautama for infidelity.
historical_references.context: The Puranas are a collection of 18 major texts and numerous minor texts. They discuss various aspects of Hindu religion, philosophy, mythology, and history.
